q1_heatmap_location.unrelated_legacy: src/streamlit_app.py operates on the v1 HybridBrainTumorModel, not FusionV2, and is out of scope

q2_method_identity.basis: GradCAMPlusPlus.get_cam_weights computes grads_power_2 / (2*grads_power_2 + sum_activations*grads_power_3 + eps), i.e. Eq. 19 of arXiv:1710.11063, whereas GradCAM.get_cam_weights is a plain spatial mean of gradients

q3_hooked_module.answer: model.cnn_stages[-1] - the final EfficientNet-B0 feature stage (index 8)

q4_differentiated_score.consequence: the differentiated scalar is the FUSED class logit model(x)[:, target_index]; it is not a branch-specific score
q4_differentiated_score.gate_in_gradient_path_reason: head() consumes fused = cat[c*g0*2, v*g1*2], and g is a differentiable function of c and v, so d(logit)/d(A_cnn) flows through both the direct c path and the gate
q4_differentiated_score.answer: the FUSED class logit is differentiated, not a branch-specific score; ClassifierOutputTarget(target_index) is applied to the full FusionV2 output

q5_preprocessing.transform_repr:
Compose(
    Resize(size=(224, 224), interpolation=bilinear, max_size=None, antialias=True)
    ToTensor()
    Normalize(mean=[0.5, 0.5, 0.5], std=[0.5, 0.5, 0.5])
)
q5_preprocessing.answer: Resize((224,224)) -> ToTensor() -> Normalize(mean=[0.5]*3, std=[0.5]*3); no CLAHE, no crop, aspect ratio not preserved

q6_spatial_resize_reversal.cam_upsampling: pytorch_grad_cam resizes the stage activation map to the INPUT tensor spatial size internally
q6_spatial_resize_reversal.display_image: the original image is resized to 224x224 with PIL BILINEAR for display - src/publication/fusion_v2_gradcam.py:136
q6_spatial_resize_reversal.consequence: the overlay is produced in 224x224 model space, NOT mapped back to the source image resolution; any spatial statement is therefore made in resized model space and inherits the resize distortion
q6_spatial_resize_reversal.normalisation_of_heatmap: min-max to [0,1] per image, zeros if constant - src/publication/fusion_v2_gradcam.py:172-176
q6_spatial_resize_reversal.answer: It is NOT reversed. The CAM is upsampled from the 7x7 stage map to the 224x224 model input grid and overlaid on a 224x224 resized copy of the image. Nothing maps the map back to the source resolution or undoes the aspect-ratio change.

q7_class_order.answer: ('glioma','meningioma','notumor','pituitary'), index 0..3, alphabetical; this matches the probability column order p_glioma..p_pituitary in the authoritative prediction CSVs and the canonical split manifest

q8_forward_graph.graph: x -> cnn_stages (taps 3,5,final; mean over H,W) -> cat(1432) -> cnn_proj -> c(512);  x -> vit.vit(...).last_hidden_state[:,0](768) -> vit_proj -> v(512);  g=softmax(gate(cat[c,v]),-1)(2); fused=cat[c*g0*2, v*g1*2](1024); logits=head(fused)(4)

q9_cnn_tensors.note: taps are pooled to vectors inside branch_features, so the SPATIAL maps are not returned by forward and must be captured with hooks
q9_cnn_tensors.answer: 9 EfficientNet stages. Multi-scale taps at index 3 (40ch, 28x28) and 5 (112ch, 14x14); final stage 8 (1280ch, 7x7). All three are pooled to vectors inside branch_features, so spatial maps are only reachable via hooks.

q10_q11_vit_tensors.answer: Available: last_hidden_state [B,197,768] and the CLS token at index 0 (the only tensor the forward pass consumes). Attention is NOT returned as loaded.

q11_attention_availability.answer: NO under the loaded configuration; YES after switching to eager attention
q11_attention_availability.transformers_warning: output_attentions=True is not supported with attn_implementation other than eager/eager_paged/flex_attention

q12_gate_input.answer: torch.cat([c, v], dim=1), the two 512-d PROJECTED BRANCH FEATURE VECTORS, shape [B,1024]
q12_gate_input.module:
Sequential(
  (0): Linear(in_features=1024, out_features=256, bias=True)
  (1): GELU(approximate='none')
  (2): Linear(in_features=256, out_features=2, bias=True)
)

q13_gate_output_kind.answer: TWO SCALAR PER-BRANCH WEIGHTS PER IMAGE, shape [B,2]. Not per-feature, not per-scale, not spatial.
q13_gate_output_kind.applied_to: the 512-d projected FEATURE VECTORS c and v, each scaled by 2*g; the gate never multiplies a spatial map

q14_gate_sums.answer: Yes. The gate is a softmax over the last dimension, so the two values sum to 1 across the branches within each image.
q14_gate_sums.sum_axis: last dimension (dim=-1), i.e. across the two branches within one image

q15_aux_logits_in_checkpoint.answer: Yes. aux_cnn and aux_vit weights and biases are present in the verified checkpoint and load under strict=True.

q16_branch_probabilities.mechanism: model(x, return_aux=True) -> (logits, aux_cnn(c), aux_vit(v), g); src/fusion_v2.py:105-106
q16_branch_probabilities.caveat: these are AUXILIARY TRAINING heads on the projected branch features; they are not the fused decision and were trained with weight 0.3 as a regulariser, so they are branch-readable proxies, not the model's output
q16_branch_probabilities.answer: Yes, without retraining: model(x, return_aux=True) returns (fused_logits, aux_cnn(c), aux_vit(v), gate). Softmax of the auxiliary logits gives per-branch class distributions. They are auxiliary regularisation heads, not the fused decision.

q21_nonintrusive_code_additions.answer: A wrapper module that instruments an already-constructed FusionV2 instance. No edit to src/fusion_v2.py is required.
mechanisms_verified_available: register_forward_hook on model.cnn_stages[i] to capture spatial maps at stages 3, 5 and 8 (verified neutral, delta 0.0)

retraining, fine-tuning or re-export of any checkpoint

q22_limitations_blocking_anatomical_clai.answer: Several, and they are structural rather than incidental.
items: No lesion masks, bounding boxes or expert annotations exist for this dataset, so there is no reference against which a map could be scored as correct.
The CNN CAM originates on a 7x7 grid and is upsampled 32x to 224x224; its effective spatial resolution is roughly 32 pixels, coarser than many lesions.
ViT attention is native 14x14 over 196 patches, a different grid from the CNN final stage, so the two paths are not spatially commensurate without resampling.
Preprocessing resizes to 224x224 without preserving aspect ratio, and the overlay is never mapped back to source resolution, so map coordinates are in distorted model space.

The reported predictions use horizontal-flip TTA (an average over two views), while the heatmap is computed from a single un-flipped forward pass, so the map does not correspond exactly to the reported probability.
Attention weights describe token mixing, not evidence for a class; treating them as an explanation is an assumption, not a result.
Gate mass measures branch utilisation only and is not causal attribution (AGENTS.md prohibits the contrary claim).
A visually plausible map is not evidence of faithfulness; only perturbation-style tests speak to that, and they test sensitivity, not anatomical correctness.

composite_formula_feasibility.question: Does the gate really produce compatible CNN and ViT branch weights, as the proposed H_composite = alpha_CNN*H_CNN + alpha_ViT*H_ViT would require?
composite_formula_feasibility.finding: PARTIALLY. The gate does emit exactly two non-negative per-image scalars summing to one, which are formally usable as alpha_CNN and alpha_ViT.
composite_formula_feasibility.but: Those scalars were trained to reweight 512-d FEATURE VECTORS before the classifier head. They were never trained to weight spatial maps, and the two maps they would weight are not the quantities the gate scales. Using them on heatmaps is an analogy, not an identity.
composite_formula_feasibility.additional_incompatibility: H_CNN is a 7x7 gradient-weighted activation map; H_ViT would be a 14x14 attention-derived map. They differ in native resolution, in units, and in normalisation, so any sum requires resampling and rescaling choices that are not determined by the model.
prohibited_terminology: evidence that the model looks at the lesion
required_before_use: state the resampling rule and the per-map normalisation explicitly
report the composite alongside its two components, never alone
treat the composite as a visualisation choice with a stated rationale, not as a derived quantity of the model
